title: Separation methods card
subject: Science
unit: Summer 1: Dissolving, separating and plants (Do All Solids Dissolve? and Allotment)
source: Seeded from science/y5 lesson 34 (Separation methods card (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 34: Getting salt back: evaporation. To understand how evaporation separates a dissolved solid from a solution

questions.q: Sand, salt and water are mixed. Put the steps in order to get dry sand and salt.
questions.a: Filter to get the sand; evaporate the filtrate to get the salt
questions.model: Step 1: what is insoluble? Sand: filter it out. Step 2: what is left? Salt water. Evaporate the water to get salt crystals.

questions.q: What leaves when salt water evaporates?
Is evaporating salt water a reversible change?
Make salty water (2 teaspoons in a little warm tap water), pour a thin layer onto a dark saucer and place on a sunny windowsill. Draw it today and again in 3 days.
questions.a: Day 1: clear liquid; day 3: white crystals on the saucer
questions.model: Teacher pours a thin layer on camera and draws the 'day 1' picture.

questions.q: Write the method for separating sand, salt and water in numbered steps.
questions.a: 1 stir in water, 2 filter, 3 evaporate the filtrate, 4 collect the salt

questions.q: Why does a thin layer on a saucer evaporate faster than a full cup?
questions.a: Larger surface area, so more water escapes at once

questions.q: Water turning into a gas is...
Big question: how do people get salt out of seawater?
questions.a: Shallow pools; the Sun evaporates the water and salt crystals are left.
